fields.acceptance: Testscripts: run start --workflow plan --new <intent> --milestone --autonomous, and run start --workflow plan --autonomous on a record change set, each exit with a usage error naming the rule and write no journal and no draft; the same starts without --autonomous run, and run start --workflow plan --new <intent> --autonomous (an intention) still runs autonomous; run resume of a plan run on a record change set whose started entry is autonomous exits with the same usage error. plan-workflow-autonomous.txtar and plan-workflow-autonomous-left.txtar, which today start an autonomous plan run on a record change set, instead start it on an intention change set (its planner adds an intent without milestone=1, served by the draft it writes, and the -left script's landed-record Decision is one landed before the run), and still check what they check now: the arbiter answering the planner's question, review rounds, the check's questions answered where they live, and the gate accepting with rule autonomous; so plan-autonomous-interview, plan-review-arbitrated and plan-gate stay verified by them
fields.statement: rhiza run start refuses --autonomous on a plan run that plans a milestone (with --milestone, for a request of kind milestone, or on an existing record change set) with a usage error naming the rule that milestone planning needs the owner, and run resume refuses to continue such a run journaled autonomous, so no milestone plan run's agent gets RHIZA_AUTONOMOUS=1

set.acceptance: A testscript ends a plan run whose change set adds an intent served by two draft change sets: normal (a record change set, landed after the interview), both are proposed, none accepted, the landed record is left as it is, and run status --json names rhiza accept --rule owner; autonomous (an intention change set, since a milestone plan never runs autonomous) with a passing review, both are accepted with rule autonomous and reasons naming the run; autonomous with a question left by the review, none is accepted and the command exits non-zero naming the question; once the arbiter's Decision answers it, both are accepted. A run on an intention change set that serves an existing intent proposes that change set itself.
